name: Branching story graph
summary: Muse writes the story as data (story-graph/1): scenes, 1-3 choices each, conditions on stats and items, effects, routes, ranked endings with a share line, and an optional choice limit. A deterministic checker walks every path (reachable scenes and endings, no dead ends, every path ends, the best ending fits the choice limit, ending odds, text per screen), then a compiler builds the game on choice_story + story_vars with a ranked score.
when_to_use: Any choose-your-own-adventure, branching story, light RPG told in scenes (gang, party, kingdom, survival day), mystery with choices, dating sim, "become X in N choices". Plan the story as a graph and let the compiler wire the engine; don't hand-write choice_story lists for these.
api: story-graph/1 {title, premise, start, max_choices?, on_limit?, vars: [{id, label, kind: stat|item|flag, init, min, max, score?}], nodes: [{id, place?, text ≤ 110 chars, enter?, choices: [{label ≤ 28, to, if?, do?, routes?: [{if, to}], note?}] | ending: {title, tone: good|secret|neutral|bad, rank, share?}}]}. Conditions: name, !name, name>=2, & and |. Effects: +name, -name, name+2, name=0. validateStoryGraph(graph) -> {ok, errors, warnings, stats}; compileStoryGraph(graph) -> {manifest, score}.

params.max_choices: int, 0 (none) to 30: every path must end within it
params.on_limit: ending node id the limit-th choice falls to
params.endings: 2-8 (aim 4-6: one rank 1, one secret, one bad)
params.vars: up to 8 (≤ 3 stats in the HUD)

gaps_it_closes: unreachable endings and dead ends in Muse-written stories
choice limits such as "in 10 choices or less"
stats, items and recruits in stories
story results a Group can compare (ending rank, choices used, share line)
notes: Built and tested (authoring/tools/test-story.mjs, 5 stories incl. 4 from real Muse). Not yet called by pipeline.mjs: see docs/harness-gaps/story.md. Prompt: authoring/expander/story-prompt.mjs; CLI: authoring/tools/story-muse.mjs.

name: Story variables
summary: The engine side of a story graph: on top of choice_story it shows only the choices whose conditions hold, applies effects to stats, items and flags (clamped), takes conditional routes, enforces a choice limit, holds the ending on screen, then wins or loses, and scores ending points + unused choices + weighted stats on ending_reached. Draws a stats line, a bag line, a place label, notes and an ending card with the share line.
when_to_use: Only through branching_story: the compiler writes its encoded lists. Never write its sg_* lists by hand.
api: requires choice_story and state lists sg_src_labels, sg_src_next, sg_need, sg_do, sg_route, sg_note (per choice), sg_enter, sg_place, sg_end_title, sg_end_tag, sg_end_points, sg_share (per scene), sg_var, sg_label, sg_kind, sg_init, sg_lo, sg_hi, sg_weight (per variable). Provides sg_vals, sg_used, sg_end, sg_share_line, sg_path, sg_score().

params.bonus: int, 25 points per unused choice on a good ending

notes: Engine-validated and replay-verified; not in the Studio bundle until it is regenerated.

name: Story stats
summary: Up to 3 visible stats in a story (coin, gang, suspicion, energy, affection) as story-graph variables: clamped to a small range, shown in the HUD, changed by choices and arrivals, gating later choices and routes, and optionally worth points at the end.
when_to_use: Light RPGs and stories where choices build something up: recruiting a gang, earning favor, a dating sim's affection, stress in a survival day. Recruits are a stat ("gang") or one item per named recruit.
api: branching_story vars: {id, label ≤ 10 chars, kind: "stat", init, min, max (span ≤ 20), score?: points per unit}. Conditions gang>=3; effects +gang, gang+2, gang=0.

name: Story playtest bots
summary: Gate bots for story games: random readers, the shortest route to the best ending, the longest run, the worst ending, and one route to every other ending, all played through the real engine and checked move by move against the story graph (scene, stats, phase, score). Their runs feed the score check, so skill order means choosing well.
when_to_use: After compiling a branching_story; in place of the generic tap bots for story games.
api: storyGate(engine, gameJson, report, manifest) -> {runs, flags, passed, summary, endings}; asScoreRuns(runs) for checkScore.

name: Story result share line
summary: The share and result text for a story run comes from the game ("I became king in 6 choices") and carries the ending id and path, so a Group can compare endings instead of raw points.
when_to_use: Every story game, so friends see endings and choice counts rather than "6125 points".
api: wanted: at the end of a run the microgame kit reads state sg_share_line, sg_end and sg_path and uses them for score_text and the result tag (ending=<id>;path=<dot path>;choices=<n>)
notes: Request for Artem (runtime kit) and Max (store the tag): docs/harness-gaps/story.md. Until then the ending card in the game shows the line and the board ranks points.
